MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which number is written in words as "two thousand and ninety"? (1 mark)
   A. 2,090
   B. 20,900
   C. 290
   D. 2,900

2. Round 205 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 310
   B. 200
   C. 210
   D. 220

3. Round 694 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 690
   B. 600
   C. 700
   D. 680

4. Which number is written in words as "seven thousand and eight"? (1 mark)
   A. 70,008
   B. 8,008
   C. 7,008
   D. 708

5. Which of these is a factor of 48? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 9
   C. 5
   D. 7

6. How many times do you need to regroup when you add 6,478 + 2,355? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 3
   C. 0
   D. 1

7. Which word in a problem tells you to subtract? (1 mark)
   A. Sum
   B. Difference
   C. Total
   D. Altogether

8. Work out 4,000 − 1,236. (1 mark)
   A. 2,664
   B. 2,764
   C. 3,236
   D. 2,774

9. Work out 36 × 24. (1 mark)
   A. 874
   B. 216
   C. 864
   D. 854

10. What is 36 × 40? (1 mark)
   A. 14,400
   B. 76
   C. 1,440
   D. 144

11. Which division fact belongs to the same family as 4 × 6 = 24? (1 mark)
   A. 24 ÷ 4 = 4
   B. 24 ÷ 4 = 6
   C. 6 ÷ 4 = 24
   D. 24 ÷ 24 = 4

12. Why must the parts be equal when we write the fraction 1/3? (1 mark)
   A. The numerator must be 3
   B. Only the shaded part must be equal
   C. The whole is cut into three parts of the same size
   D. The parts can be any size

13. Which fraction of an hour is 30 minutes? (1 mark)
   A. 1/4
   B. 1/3
   C. 3/4
   D. 1/2

14. What is 7/10 of 20? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 2
   C. 16
   D. 14

15. Write 5/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 5.0
   B. 0.05
   C. 0.5
   D. 0.005

16. Write 27/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.027
   B. 2.7
   C. 0.27
   D. 0.72

17. Write 3/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 3.0
   B. 0.03
   C. 0.13
   D. 0.3

18. A hundred square has 35 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 35
   B. 0.035
   C. 3.5
   D. 0.35

19. Which is greater, 0.6 or 0.06? (1 mark)
   A. 0.06
   B. They are equal
   C. 0.6
   D. It cannot be told

20. Simplify 4b + 3b. (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 43b
   C. 12b
   D. 7b

21. A square has sides of 15 m. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 30 m
   B. 60 m
   C. 45 m
   D. 225 m

22. Change 2 m 45 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 65 cm
   B. 2,450 cm
   C. 245 cm
   D. 47 cm

23. A rectangle is made of 3 rows with 5 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 15 square units
   B. 8 square units
   C. 18 square units
   D. 16 square units

24. A square is covered with 10 rows of 10 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 40 square units
   B. 100 square units
   C. 20 square units
   D. 110 square units

25. A cuboid is 4 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 28 blocks
   B. 24 blocks
   C. 9 blocks
   D. 12 blocks

26. What is 4 1/2 L + 2 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 7 1/2 L
   B. 7 1/4 L
   C. 7 L
   D. 6 3/4 L

27. What is 10 L − 4 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 6 L
   B. 5 1/2 L
   C. 5 3/4 L
   D. 6 1/4 L

28. How many 1/4 kg masses balance a 1 kg mass? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 3
   C. 8
   D. 4

29. How long is a lesson that starts at 9:30 a.m. and ends at 12:10 p.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 50 min
   B. 3 h 40 min
   C. 2 h 25 min
   D. 2 h 40 min

30. What is 3 h 50 min + 2 h 25 min? (1 mark)
   A. 5 h 15 min
   B. 6 h 25 min
   C. 6 h 5 min
   D. 6 h 15 min

31. Change 17 days to weeks and days. (1 mark)
   A. 3 weeks
   B. 2 weeks 4 days
   C. 3 weeks 2 days
   D. 2 weeks 3 days

32. Change 28 days to weeks and days. (1 mark)
   A. 4 weeks
   B. 4 weeks 1 days
   C. 5 weeks
   D. 0 weeks 4 days

33. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 9 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 6. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 9:30
   B. 9:06
   C. 10:30
   D. 6:45

34. Kip faces South and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. South
   C. East
   D. West

35. How many corners does a cuboid have? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 4
   C. 12
   D. 6

36. A gate opens through a quarter turn from the wall. What angle does it make with the wall? (1 mark)
   A. A straight line
   B. No angle
   C. A full turn
   D. A right angle

37. At 3 o'clock the hands of a clock make (1 mark)
   A. a straight line
   B. a full turn
   C. a very small angle
   D. a right angle

38. Which statement about a rectangle is true? (1 mark)
   A. It has a curved edge
   B. All sides are always equal
   C. Opposite sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   D. It has three sides

39. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 10
   C. 11
   D. 12

40. In a tally chart, one group of five and 1 more single tally mark are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 11
   C. 5
   D. 6

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Add 4,236 and 1,528. Show your working. (3 marks)

42. Find the area of a square with 6 rows of 6 unit squares. Then find the area of a rectangle with 5 rows of 7 squares. Which is bigger? (4 marks)

43. Explain why multiplying by 100 puts two zeros on the end of a whole number. (3 marks)

44. Work out 12 × 21 showing both partial products. (3 marks)

45. Estimate 7,483 − 2,196 by rounding to the nearest ten. Then find the exact answer. (4 marks)

46. Amina faces north. She makes a half turn, then a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does she face at the end? (4 marks)

47. Name two things at home or school that are turned clockwise to tighten or close them. (2 marks)

48. Work out 6,003 − 2,475 and check your answer by adding. (4 marks)

49. On a poultry farm each of 16 hens lays 21 eggs in one month. How many eggs are laid altogether? (3 marks)

50. Arrange 605, 560, 650 and 506 from smallest to largest. (3 marks)

51. A lesson starts at 8:15 a.m. and ends at 10:40 a.m. How long is the lesson? (3 marks)

52. A 20 L jerrycan is used to fill 5 L buckets. How many buckets can be filled? How many 1/4 L cups can be filled from one bucket? (4 marks)

53. Subtract 2,718 from 5,432, showing every regrouping step. (4 marks)

54. State whether 1,468 and 3,975 are even or odd. Give a reason for each. (3 marks)

55. Explain why 0.5 is greater than 0.45 even though 0.45 has more digits. (3 marks)

56. Explain why you should read a measuring jug at the same height as the water. (2 marks)

57. Tabitha cuts a 7 m 20 cm rope into 6 pieces of equal length. Find the length of one piece. (3 marks)

58. Give two differences between perimeter and area. (3 marks)

59. Share 96 metres of rope equally into pieces of 8 metres. How many pieces are there? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 2,090
   two thousand and ninety: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 2,090.

2. C — 210
   Look at the ones digit 5. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 205 rounds to 210.

3. A — 690
   Look at the ones digit 4. It is less than 5, so keep the tens digit. 694 rounds to 690.

4. C — 7,008
   seven thousand and eight: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 7,008.

5. A — 12
   48 ÷ 12 = 4 with nothing left over, so 12 is a factor of 48. The others leave a remainder.

6. A — 2
   Check each column from the right for a total of 10 or more, remembering the carried digit. 6,478 + 2,355 needs 2 regroupings.

7. B — Difference
   Difference means how much bigger one number is than the other, so we subtract.

8. B — 2,764
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 4,000 − 1,236 = 2,764. Check: 2,764 + 1,236 = 4,000.

9. C — 864
   36 × 4 = 144 and 36 × 20 = 720. 144 + 720 = 864.

10. C — 1,440
   36 × 4 = 144, then × 10 gives 1,440.

11. B — 24 ÷ 4 = 6
   Division undoes multiplication. Since 4 × 6 = 24, we know 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

12. C — The whole is cut into three parts of the same size
   A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. If the parts are different sizes, one part is not one third.

13. D — 1/2
   There are 60 minutes in an hour. 30 minutes is half of 60, so it is 1/2 of an hour.

14. D — 14
   20 ÷ 10 = 2 and 2 × 7 = 14. So 7/10 of 20 is 14.

15. B — 0.05
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 5/100 = 0.05.

16. C — 0.27
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 27/100 = 0.27.

17. D — 0.3
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 3/10 = 0.3.

18. D — 0.35
   35 out of 100 squares is 35/100 = 0.35.

19. C — 0.6
   Compare the tenths first. 0.6 is greater than 0.06.

20. D — 7b
   Only like terms can be joined. 4b + 3b = 7b.

21. B — 60 m
   A square has four equal sides. 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60.

22. C — 245 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 2 × 100 = 200, and 200 + 45 = 245. So the answer is 245 cm.

23. A — 15 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 3 × 5 = 15 square units.

24. B — 100 square units
   Area = 10 × 10 = 100 square units.

25. B — 24 blocks
   One layer has 4 × 3 = 12 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 12 × 2 = 24 blocks.

26. C — 7 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 4 1/2 L + 2 1/2 L = 7 L.

27. C — 5 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 10 L − 4 1/4 L = 5 3/4 L.

28. D — 4
   Four quarters make one whole kilogram.

29. D — 2 h 40 min
   Count on from 9:30 a.m. to 12:10 p.m.. The total is 2 h 40 min.

30. D — 6 h 15 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 6 h 15 min.

31. D — 2 weeks 3 days
   17 ÷ 7 = 2 remainder 3, so 17 days = 2 weeks 3 days.

32. A — 4 weeks
   28 ÷ 7 = 4 remainder 0, so 28 days = 4 weeks.

33. A — 9:30
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 6 shows 6 × 5 = 30 minutes, so the time is 9:30.

34. D — West
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. South followed by a quarter turn clockwise gives West.

35. A — 8
   A cuboid such as a matchbox has 8 corners.

36. D — A right angle
   A quarter turn makes a right angle.

37. D — a right angle
   At 3 o'clock the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand at 3, a quarter turn apart.

38. C — Opposite sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   A rectangle has four sides, opposite sides equal and four right angles.

39. B — 10
   Add all the numbers: 5 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 10.

40. D — 6
   1 × 5 + 1 = 6.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 5,764
   Working / marking points: Ones 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 carry 1 (1 mark); tens 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 (1 mark); hundreds 2 + 5 = 7, thousands 4 + 1 = 5, answer 5,764 (1 mark).

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Square 36, rectangle 35. The square is bigger by 1 square unit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each area and 1 mark for the comparison and 1 mark for the difference.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each digit moves two places to the left, so it becomes 100 times bigger. The empty tens and ones places are filled with zeros.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for digits moving two places, 1 mark for 100 times bigger, 1 mark for zeros filling places.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 252
   Working / marking points: 12 × 1 = 12 (1 mark); 12 × 20 = 240 (1 mark); 12 + 240 = 252 (1 mark).

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 7,480 − 2,200 = 5,280. Exact: 5,287.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rounded number, 1 mark for 5,280, 1 mark for 5,287.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: East
   Working / marking points: A half turn from north gives south (2 marks). A quarter turn anticlockwise from south gives east (2 marks).

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two, for example a bottle top or a screw, and a tap being closed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3,528. Check: 3,528 + 2,475 = 6,003.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for correct regrouping across the zeros, 1 mark for the answer, 1 mark for the check.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: 336 eggs
   Working / marking points: 21 × 6 = 126 (1 mark); 21 × 10 = 210 (1 mark); 126 + 210 = 336 (1 mark).

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: 506, 560, 605, 650
   Working / marking points: Compare hundreds first, then tens. 1 mark for each correct pair of positions, up to 3 marks.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 25 minutes
   Working / marking points: 8:15 to 10:15 is 2 hours (1 mark); 10:15 to 10:40 is 25 minutes (1 mark); total 2 h 25 min (1 mark).

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4 buckets; 20 cups
   Working / marking points: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 (2 marks); 5 × 4 = 20 cups (2 marks).

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: 2,714
   Working / marking points: Ones 12 − 8 = 4 (1 mark); tens 2 − 1 = 1 (1 mark); hundreds 14 − 7 = 7 (1 mark); thousands 4 − 2 = 2 (1 mark).

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,468 is even because it ends in 8. 3,975 is odd because it ends in 5.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct classification with a reason (2 marks) and 1 mark for referring to the ones digit.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.5 = 0.50. Comparing tenths, 5 tenths is more than 4 tenths, so 0.50 is greater than 0.45. The number of digits does not decide the size.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for writing 0.5 as 0.50, 1 mark for comparing tenths, 1 mark for the conclusion.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Looking from above or below makes the water level seem to be at a different mark, so the reading would be wrong.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying the reading can be wrong and 1 mark for the reason.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 m 20 cm
   Working / marking points: 720 ÷ 6 = 120 cm (2 marks); 120 cm = 1 m 20 cm (1 mark).

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Perimeter is the distance round the edge and is measured in units of length such as cm. Area is the flat surface inside the shape and is measured in square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning of each and 1 mark for the units.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: 12 pieces
   Working / marking points: 96 ÷ 8 = 12. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.
